who: Japanese proverb · Ishi no ue ni mo sannen
quote: Three years, even on a stone.
meaning: Stay long enough, and even a cold stone gets warm.

quote: There was a man of Sung, who was grieved that his growing corn was not longer, and so he pulled it up. ... 'I have been helping the corn to grow long.' His son ran to look at it, and found the corn all withered.
meaning: He pulled his young plants up to help them grow faster. Soon they had all dried up.

quote: Do not be desirous to have things done quickly... Desire to have things done quickly prevents their being done thoroughly.
meaning: If you want things done fast, they will not be done well.

who: Kabir · couplet on patience, 15th century, tr. from Hindi
quote: Slowly, slowly, O mind; everything happens slowly. The gardener pours a hundred pots of water, but fruit comes when its season comes.
meaning: A hundred pots of water won't bring the fruit early. It comes in its season.

who: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 2, tr. Richard M. Gummere, 1917
quote: Everywhere means nowhere... nothing hinders a cure so much as frequent change of medicine; no wound will heal when one salve is tried after another; a plant which is often moved can never grow strong.
meaning: If you keep changing the method, nothing has time to work. A plant moved too often never grows strong.

who: Laozi · Dao De Jing 15, tr. James Legge, 1891
quote: Who can (make) the muddy water (clear)? Let it be still, and it will gradually become clear. Who can secure the condition of rest? Let movement go on, and the condition of rest will gradually arise.
meaning: Leave muddy water still, and it slowly clears. Keep moving gently, and calm slowly comes.

who: Krishna · Bhagavad Gita 2.47, tr. K. T. Telang, 1882
quote: Your business is with action alone; not by any means with fruit. Let not the fruit of action be your motive (to action).
meaning: Your job is the doing. Don't do it for the result. The result is not your business.

who: Henri Poincaré · Science and Method, 1908, tr. G. B. Halsted, 1913
quote: Disgusted with my failure, I went to spend a few days at the seaside, and thought of something else. One morning, walking on the bluff, the idea came to me...
meaning: He stopped forcing the problem and rested by the sea. Then the answer came by itself.

who: Russian proverb · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: The slower you go, the farther you get.
meaning: Slow and steady goes farther than a rush.

who: Rainer Maria Rilke · Letters to a Young Poet, 1903, tr. M. D. Herter Norton, 1934
quote: ...ripening like the tree which does not force its sap and stands confident in the storms of spring without the fear that after them may come no summer. It does come. But it comes only to the patient...
meaning: Grow like a tree that does not rush. Summer will come, but only to people who wait.
